styles.label: History
styles.blurb: The first cathedral, fortress and cobbled streets of the New World.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Mangú breakfasts, street snacks and criollo dinners.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, colonial plazas and live merengue after dark.

stays.why: Walk to the cathedral, Alcázar and Plaza España. Best for first-timers who want history on foot.
Modern business district with the best restaurants and malls. Quieter nights, short taxi rides to the old city.
Leafy, calm streets between the Colonial Zone and the Malecón. Good value and walkable to both.
Residential area near the Malecón with apartments and mid-range hotels. Easy for longer stays.

food: Start the day with mangú: mashed plantain with eggs, fried cheese and salami. Cheap and filling.
Try Dominican classics: la bandera (rice, beans, meat), sancocho stew and tostones.
Street snacks: empanadas, quipes and chimi burgers. Eat where locals queue; prices are low.
Seafood along the Malecón and in Boca Chica. Ask the price before ordering fish by weight.
Coffee is strong and local. Look for small cafés in the Zona Colonial; a cup is a few hundred DOP at most.
more_time: Add a beach day: Boca Chica is about 30–40 minutes east by taxi or bus. Check conditions on the day.
History buffs can swap a museum for the Faro a Colón and the Columbus sites across the Ozama river.
Take a day trip to Los Tres Ojos caves and the Botanical Garden if you want nature close to the city.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the Colonial Zone and the Malecón at an easy pace. Add a night for a beach day or nightlife.

month_notes: January: dry-ish and mild, highs near 28°C. Great for walking the old city.
February: similar to January, around 29°C. Comfortable sightseeing weather.
March: warm at 29°C with about 14 rain days. Carry a light rain jacket.
April: warmer and wetter, about 18 rain days. Plan indoor sights for afternoons.
May: rainy season builds, about 22 rain days. Short heavy showers are common.
June: hot and wet, highs near 30°C. Go out early and stay shaded at midday.
July: hottest month, highs around 31°C, still rainy. Hydrate and use sunscreen.
August: hot and very wet, about 23 rain days. Expect afternoon downpours.
September: hot and rainy, around 30°C. Hurricane season peaks; watch forecasts.
October: still wet, about 20 rain days. Slightly cooler evenings.
November: rain eases to about 19 days. Pleasant for the city and the Malecón.
December: cooler and drier, highs near 28°C. One of the best months to visit.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical climate: warm all year, with a wetter season from May to October and a drier, slightly cooler stretch from November to April.

items.title: Best time: December to March
items.text: Highs around 28–29°C and fewer rain days. Ideal for walking the Colonial Zone.

items.title: Wet season: May to October
items.text: About 20–23 rain days a month. Showers are often short and heavy; plan around them.

items.title: Hottest months: July and August
items.text: Highs near 31°C with warm nights around 24°C. Go out early or after sunset.

items.title: Hurricane season: June to November
items.text: Peaks around September. Check forecasts and keep plans flexible.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light, breathable clothes, a rain jacket or umbrella, sunscreen and a hat. A light layer for air-conditioned museums.

items.title: Rain timing
items.text: Downpours often come in the afternoon. Do outdoor sights in the morning and keep a backup indoor plan.

transit.best: Walk the Zona Colonial and Malecón; use Uber or InDrive for longer trips.

modes.text: Two lines, RD$20 per ride with a smartcard (RD$60 card plus RD$20 minimum). Useful for some cross-city trips.
Cheap but confusing; fares around RD$20–40. Fine if you have time and local help.
Taxis have no meters, so agree the fare before you get in. Uber and InDrive work and are often easier.
Driving is chaotic; not recommended for short visits.
Best in the Zona Colonial and along the Malecón. Sidewalks are uneven, so watch your step.
Ferry to Puerto Rico (Mayagüez or San Juan) is about US$200 roundtrip and takes around 12 hours.
